transcription.full_text: Look at this shit. Haiti forced to change World Cup jerseys after FIFA rejects political elements. In a statement responding to the decision, Kit manufacturer say to confirm that it would work, it had worked with FIFA to ensure the design would meet requirements, even having successfully implemented the requested modifications during the mandatory review. Working in close collaboration with the Haitian Football Federation, say to statement elaborated our objective throughout the process was to create a jersey that celebrated the pride, resilience and spirit of the Haitian people. Following the review process, FIFA determined that certain visual elements could be interpreted differently under its equipment regulations and ultimately requested modifications to the design. While the interpretation deferred from our intention, we remain proud to have contributed alongside the Haitian Football League. And a lot of you still don't believe that the game isn't completely rigged. For 52 years, Haiti has been locked out, isolated and pushed to the margins of the global stage. 52 years of being denied a real fair shot, unable to even play on their own home soil because of the endless instability fueled by global politics. And the exact moment they finally scraped together something of their own, the exact second they step up to claim their rightful place in the 2026 World Cup qualifiers, the institutions immediately target them. FIFA steps in and bans their jersey, calling a tiny piece of artwork in the corner to political. It's a small, quiet image of a man holding a flag representing the Haitian Revolution and their fight for independence. That is their history. It is a literal historical fact. But when Haiti wants to wear the truth of how they broke their own chains, the gatekeepers panic and branded a violation. Where are the major brands? Where was Nike, Adidas, Reebok or Jordan? Nowhere. They didn't hop on the bandwagon to help Haiti design or fund a custom kit. They didn't care. Haiti had to do every single bit of this themselves. They built something out of nothing entirely on their own terms and the immediate response from the powers above is to shut it down. It feels like they are systemically targeted so they can't have anything to call their own. The jersey is loud enough to make you laugh if it wasn't so sickening. When the United States celebrates the 4th of July, turns Independence Day into a massive national holiday and floods stadiums with people dressed as George Washington or Abraham Lincoln cheering USA, USA, nobody blinks. No one says that's too political. That's okay, right? I mean, the US got its independence by fighting a war against the United Kingdom. And England is out here playing in the exact same tournaments without a single issue. Colonial history and Western nationalism are treated as default, neutral and celebrated. But the moment a black republic honors its own survival, it's treated as a dangerous political statement. And this is not about regulations or uniform guidelines. This is about a psychological embargo that has been running for over two centuries. The root cause of this hatred, this constant targeting, is that Haiti committed the ultimate unpardonable sin in the eyes of the Western world. They won. They didn't ask for permission. They didn't negotiate a treaty for gradual freedom. They broke their own chains, looked the most powerful evil empires on earth in the eye and took their liberty by force. And the global system has spent every single day since 1804 making sure they pay for that audacity. And then we got to look at the sickening hypocrisy of what they choose to call political. When the United States or England steps onto a pitch, draped in the symbols of empires built on colonial theft, bloody expansion and subjugation, it's called national pride. They can sing anthems born from war, turn their flags into global marketing campaigns, and turn national holidays into worldwide spectacles. But the moment Haiti puts a tiny quiet piece of artwork in the corner of a shirt, in the corner of a jersey, just a man holding up a flag, a mirror to the reality of how they achieve survival, the gatekeepers panic. Why? Because a black man holding a flag of self liberation is a threat to the narrative they've built. They want Haiti to be seen exclusively through the lens of pain, disaster, poverty and foreign intervention. They want a version of Haiti that looks broken because a broken nation justifies their savior complex. But they absolutely cannot tolerate is a Haiti that stands up on the world stage and reminds everybody where true revolution comes from. They don't teach this in schools because if people knew the truth about 1804, the whole deck of cards would fall. They don't want the world to know that the wealth of the West was paid for by the deliberate systemic strangulation of the first independent black republic. I mean, for 52 years, Haiti has been locked out, unable to play on their own home soil, isolated by travel bands, abandoned by the massive corporate entities like Nike, Adidas or Jordan, who love to extract black culture for profit, but look the other way when actual black sovereignty needs a platform. Haiti had to do this entirely alone. They built their own kit, found their own way, and the absolute second they stood up to claim their fair opportunity, the system tried to cut them down at the knees. It's selective amnesia. It's a calculated attempt to keep a people invisible. It's selective censorship. Parents simple. They don't want the world to truly know or look at that history, which is the exact same reason they completely erase it and refuse to teach it in schools. Combined with the recent constant travel bands slapped on Haitian tours. It's just been hit after hit after hit against these people. I'm not even Haitian myself, but just watching this makes my blood boil. It's a brutal, exhausting reminder that the system is set up to keep them invisible, and it feels like the entire world is constantly aligned against them. And the solution to this psychological warfare is not to beg FIFA for compliance or alter the artwork to make the colonizer comfortable. The solution is to realize that the jersey was never just a shirt. It's an eviction notice to their hypocrisy. If they banned the symbol on the pitch, then the diaspora must put that symbol on every street corner, every stadium seat, every screen, and every back across the globe. You can't censor a legacy that is etched into the bone. They wanted to hide the flag, but all they did was prove to the world how terrified they still are of the people who shook the earth to be free.
